research.recommended_topic: Last-minute March 31 tax-saving traps: Why buying traditional insurance/ULIPs in panic ruins your wealth
research.audience_problem: Young salaried Indian professionals face urgent financial year-end proof deadlines and succumb to aggressive pitches from bank relationship managers and relatives for low-yield, long-lock-in insurance policies.
research.why_now: The March 31 financial year deadline creates immediate urgency, peak search interest in Section 80C deductions, and high financial anxiety among corporate employees.
research.hook: Stop! Before you buy that 'tax-saving insurance plan' your uncle or bank RM is pitching this week, watch this.
supporting_points: Traditional endowment and money-back policies consistently yield an XIRR of only 4.5% to 5.5%, failing to beat long-term retail inflation in India.
Evaluating the New Tax Regime first: If total deductions don't exceed the breakeven threshold, forced lock-in investments are entirely unnecessary.
The clean separation rule: Buy pure term insurance for risk protection and allocate tax-saving funds to PPF or 3-year ELSS rather than 15-year rigid commitments.
trend_signals: March 31 Financial Year-End tax-proof cycle across Indian corporate sectors
Spike in Google Trends for '80C investment options' and 'Old vs New Regime calculator'
Trending Indian creator format: 'POV: Your bank RM in late March' relatable skit reel hook
High save-to-reach ratio on carousel breakdowns comparing policy returns against basic index funds
candidate_topics: Old vs New Tax Regime: The exact salary threshold where switching makes you richer in 2025
Credit card miles strategy: Booking affordable summer travel before peak April-May surge
The micro-spending leak: How IPL fantasy apps and quick-commerce snacking eat your month-end surplus
research.reasoning: The topic capitalizes on unavoidable calendar-driven panic with high emotional resonance in the Indian corporate ecosystem. It delivers clear actionable value, naturally drives saves and shares to peer/family groups, and establishes authority by countering predatory financial selling practices.

carousel_outline: Slide 1 (Cover / Hook): 'Salary aayi nahi ki gayab?' Why your bank balance hits rock bottom by week two (and how to fix it).
Slide 2: Mistake 1 - The 'Treat Yourself' Overdose. Celebrating payday before clearing mandatory essentials.
Slide 3: Mistake 2 - The Credit Card Illusion. Treating card limits as bonus income instead of high-interest debt.
Slide 4: The 48-Hour Rule. Putting a mandatory pause on non-essential online checkout carts.
Slide 5: Desi 50-30-20 Rule. Balancing high rent in Bangalore or Mumbai without killing your weekend chai and cafe plans.
Slide 6: Mistake 3 - 'Kuch hoga toh dekha jayega'. Why waiting to build an emergency fund always backfires.
Slide 7: 3 Actionable Automations. SIPs, recurring deposits, and bill payments to schedule on Day 1.
Slide 8 (Final Slide): Save this checklist before the 1st of the month & send it to your work bestie!
